chunks: Ibn Mahbub narrated from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Burayd ibn Mu'awiyah, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far عليه السلام about a man who performed ẓihār against his wife and then divorced her with one divorce. He said: "If he divorces her with one divorce, then the ẓihār has become null, and the divorce has demolished the ẓihār."
So I said to him: "Does he have the right to take her back?" He said: "Yes, she is his wife. So if he takes her back, what is required of one who has performed ẓihār becomes obligatory upon him."
I said: "If he leaves her until her term ends and she comes to possess herself, then he marries her after that, does the ẓihār remain binding upon him"
He said: "No. She has separated from him and has come to possess herself."

I said: "If he performs ẓihār against her, then does not touch her, and leaves her without touching her, except that he sees her uncovered without touching her, does anything become obligatory upon him in that?" He said: "She is his wife, and intercourse with her is not forbidden to him; however, what is required of one who has performed ẓihār becomes obligatory upon him before he has intercourse with her, while she is his wife."

I said: "If she raises the matter to the authority and says: 'This is my husband; he has performed ẓihār against me and is keeping me without touching me, fearing that what is required of one who has performed ẓihār would become obligatory upon him,' then what?" He said: "It is not required of him that he be compelled to emancipation, fasting, and feeding if he does not have what he may emancipate, is not able to fast, and does not find what he may give in charity. But if he is able to emancipate, then it is upon the Imam to compel him to emancipation and charity before he touches her and after he touches her."

key_terms.السُّلْطَانِ: the governing authority before whom the complaint is raised
key_terms.الظِّهَارُ: Ẓihār, the pre-Islamic form of declaring one’s wife like a prohibited relative, carrying legal consequences
key_terms.الْمُظَاهِرِ: the man who has performed ẓihār
key_terms.يَتَمَاسّٰا: to touch one another, meaning marital intercourse in this legal context
key_terms.يُرَاجِعَهَا: to take her back during the revocable waiting period

ai.seo_question: What happens to ẓihār if a man divorces his wife and then takes her back or remarries her?
ai.summary: This hadith explains several legal rulings concerning ẓihār within marriage and after divorce. It clarifies when ẓihār is nullified, when its kaffarah remains due before marital relations, and the role of the Imam or authority in compelling compliance when the husband has the means.
